newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN investigator reminds of unsolved Zaire killings.
newsitem.headline: UN investigator reminds of unsolved Zaire killings.

text.p: With Zaire's rebel forces about to take over the entire country, a U.N. human rights investigator reminded reporters on Friday of abortive international probes into reported massacres in rebel areas.

Jonas Foli of Ghana disclosed to reporters in detail the reasons officials from Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire gave earlier this month for turning down a U.N. human rights probe on missing Rwandan civilian refugees.

The alliance, he said, gave four reasons: it did not want Roberto Garreton, the Chilean head of the mission included; it wanted its own lawyer, army officer, forensic expert and surgeon in the mission; it wanted 2-3 observers from the Organisation of African Unity; it wanted to vet the backgrounds of all Argentine forensic experts in the group.
Foli said the alliance had known the group was coming and had given them the green light but its "general commissioner for justice" in Goma refused to even talk to an advance party.

"They had known of our coming. They had not raised any objections at all," he said. "And when we got there they made it impossible for us to go in and wanted us to change the commission's mandate. We tried to meet them half way but they would not accept anything from us."

The group instead waited in Kigali in neighbouring Rwanda, a strong backer of Kabila, before returning home. The refugees fled to Zaire after the 1994 genocide of minority Tutsis, which then took over the Rwanda government.
